title: Scalable Traffic Signal Control with Shared Policy Framework
claim: Global sharing ignores heterogeneity and group sharing uses static observations; ours groups units flexibly using policy-aware patterns including actions.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right (a)(b)(c), progressive evolution, shared cluster-with-star motif
description: Three side-by-side panels compare parameter-sharing schemes for traffic signal control, each captioned below. (a) CoLight: a single local observation vector (one light-blue cell) points via dashed arrows to scattered black dots inside one large yellow ellipse with a single orange star, representing one global policy. (b) GPLight: a three-cell blue observation bracket points to dots in three colored clusters (green Group 1, blue Group 3, purple Group 2), each with its own orange star. The labeled 'TSC Policy' star and a red dot show group membership. (c) SLight: the observation bracket is extended with an orange action vector (policy-determined actions). Compact groups are shown with stars, and an orange dashed arrow links a star back to the action vector. The progression from one blob to groups to policy-aware groups guides the eye left to right.
caption: Comparison of Co-Light, GPLight, and our SLight
abstract: Learning-based Traffic Signal Control (TSC) achieves satisfactory performance in small networks, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in larger networks under dynamic traffic patterns and intersection heterogeneity. In this work, we propose SLight, a policy-aware grouped MARL-TSC framework that enables scalability and efficiency balance under dynamic and heterogeneous traffic conditions. SLight captures policy-influenced traffic patterns with a policy-aware traffic pattern encoder, learns explicit group-level shared control principles from state–action trajectories, and matches each intersection’s traffic pattern embedding to principle prototypes flexibly through a compatibility-based adaptive assignment module. Experiments on real-world and synthetic networks demonstrate that SLight sustains performance gains as scale increases and outperforms existing rule-based, reinforcement learning, and grouping-based baselines. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/MaHaoLun/Slight-code.git}
